decision: Keep the CUDA kernel modes as opt-in research options of the frame API: coarse ncc_mode 3 (exact Q28 tiles with binary32 screening) with fine NCC mode 2 (row-wise Q28 sampling) on transfer mode 3 is the recommended CUDA frame setting for research runs. Transfer bit 4 (upload the fine requests) and several copy threads are kept as options but not recommended; coarse ncc_mode 4 / fine mode 3 stay an inexact ablation. Defaults, the core and the GUI are unchanged.

hypotheses.H5: held (4344/4344 CPU matches found, 0 extra; worst score 1.35e-5, center 0.00123 px, angle 0.00145 degree; 8/408 runs bit-identical)

failures_and_disclosures.what: first screening version sent 42% of the windows to binary64 (development, before registration)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: canvas border windows have zero variance and failed the screening condition
failures_and_disclosures.fix: zero-variance windows get the exact score 0 that normalizeScore() returns; mutant K13 added; 0.11% of the formal windows are scored in binary64

failures_and_disclosures.what: first coarseQ28 version requested the whole opt-in shared memory (development)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: launch failed with invalid argument because the kernel also has static shared counters; the fine sampling variants differ in static shared memory as well
failures_and_disclosures.fix: coarseQ28's dynamic limit is opt-in minus its static size; the fine budget uses the largest static size of the three variants

failures_and_disclosures.effect: the waiting script polled formal.log every 60 s until timing-start appeared, so it read it once within 60 s after timing began (round 0, warm-up, not in the summary); then every 20 minutes (around rounds 3 and 7) and once after the end; each poll read the whole formal.log (under 200 bytes), not one line as the protocol said; no other connection to the PC during timing

failures_and_disclosures.what: fp32 ablation is not bit-identical (8/408 runs identical)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: expected for the inexact ablation; H5 measures the distances; Src10 subpixel swaps the order of near-tied matches in all 8 rounds

failures_and_disclosures.what: f2 alone not faster on every case in default and FastMode (14/17, 12/17)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: descriptive arm; the cases with light fine search (Src10, some Src5) gain nothing

ungated_mutants.U1: survived, as in the transfer step (no system fence before the completion signal; PCIe posted writes arrive in order on this host). The fence stays.
ungated_mutants.U2: survived, as in the transfer step (prepare does not wait for the previous upload; the CPU copy is slower than the previous DMA). The wait stays.
ungated_mutants.U5: survived as expected: without the zero-variance rule those windows go to binary64, where normalizeScore() also returns 0; outputs unchanged, only slower

findings_posthoc.mapped_requests: Src6 subpixel fineStripes per launch: m0 780.3 us, m3 830.9 us, u7 800.1 us; about 60% of the lean-call kernel slowdown is the request read from mapped memory, but u7's extra copy costs 39 us more per fine call on the host
findings_posthoc.copy_threads: with four copy threads the source uploads ran at 15-18 GB/s (2 MiB chunks) and 2.7-3.6 GB/s (last chunk) instead of 32-42 GB/s, although every chunk is queued only after all its shares are copied; the cause (freshly written lines in several cores' caches) is a guess, not verified

limits: one GPU (RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell), one driver (596.71, WDDM), Windows only
frame API only; the handle API is unchanged
binary32 screening needs templates of at most 1e6 pixels; larger templates are not screened
small images (Src3, Src8, Src9) are dominated by fixed per-frame costs; no CUDA Graphs
after this step the coarse kernel is bound by byte-wise shared-memory reads and the fine kernel by 33% occupancy; dp4a words and int8 Tensor cores have not been tried
17 fixed fixtures only; no many-object or 8K scenes
